items.title: Investigation by plaintiffs' law firms (led by Pomerantz LLP) into possible securities fraud, following an FDA safety alert (30/06/2025) flagging a potential risk of severe CIDP worsening on VYVGART Hytrulo (based on FAERS reports); the stock had fallen 1,6% on the day of the alert.
items.allegedBy: Plaintiffs' law firms (Pomerantz LLP, among others)
items.source: Pomerantz LLP PRNewswire/GlobeNewswire press releases (July-August 2025); no formally filed complaint found as at the date of this refresh (status unchanged since the investigation was opened, no confirmed escalation into a class action)

compliance.note: A single item identified, still at the preliminary investigation stage with no confirmed complaint filed (unlike other Pomerantz matters from the same period where a class action was formally announced). To be re-checked at a future refresh if the status changes.

suiviNarratif: Readout of the Phase 2 DGF data came between the two calls: in Q1, the CMO presented the Phase 2 DGF study as one that still had to inform a Phase 3 decision; in Q2, once the data had been read, he explicitly confirms that they do NOT support a DGF indication (interesting signal on renal parameters but insufficient), while specifying that no causal link is to be drawn with the separate MMN programme - a shift expected and explained by the arrival of the data, not a reversal of the narrative.

Success framework for the myositis readout unchanged from one quarter to the next: as early as Q1, management defined success as statistical significance in at least one subgroup (IMNM or DM), each subtype having 'its own chance of succeeding'; that framing, repeated identically in Q2 just ahead of the readout, was borne out on 17/08 (IMNM significant p=0,0048, DM positive but not significant p=0,1093) - narrative entirely consistent with the outcome.

The ocular MG theme moved markedly up in importance between the two calls: a mere mention in Q1, in Q2 it becomes a theme in its own right with an explicitly reinforced tone of confidence ('very confident') presented as a new long-term growth driver.

Vision 2030 and guidance discipline unchanged across both quarters: still no quantified revenue/EPS guidance (biotech convention maintained), qualitative targets (50 000 patients, 10 indications, 5 late-stage candidates) reaffirmed identically.

clesRetenues: Q Anupam Rama (Guggenheim) - strategic direction under the new CEO: Vision 2030 confirmed unchanged (2,5x more VYVGART patients, 3x more indications, 5 late-stage molecules); broadened MG label expected to be the widest in the sector, VYVGART already chosen 4 times out of 5 as first biologic.

Q Tazeen Ahmad (BofA) - probability of success by subtype in myositis: the three subtypes rest on solid biology, any statistical significance on the primary endpoint would be considered a success; DM remains an area of high unmet need, IMNM broader than anticipated (~20 000 patients) but DM retains room for several mechanisms.

Q Derek Archila (Wells Fargo) - expectations for revenue progression in Q2 26: annual guidance unchanged, very solid underlying demand trends with steady sequential growth; the myositis primary endpoint (mean TIS score at week 52) will be reported, with subtype contextualisation details reserved for medical congresses.

Q James Gordon (Barclays) - UPLIZNA competition in MG: recent competitors are positioning in later lines/refractory patients, VYVGART keeps its focus on early treatment (80% of the MG market still non-biologic); C5 competitor impact mainly in refractory, VYVGART's first-line position intact.
Q Alex Thompson (Stifel) - appetite for business development: broadening beyond academic partnerships, strategic investments (Fortay, Tensegrity) in novel biology alongside internal innovation.

Q Rajan Sharma (Goldman Sachs) - perspective on the J&J head-to-head trial: argenx sets the efficacy/safety standards, with a focus on value through innovations such as the pre-filled syringe; operating leverage expected every quarter and every year despite the investment in innovation.

Q Allison Bratzel (Piper Sandler) - go/no-go criteria for the Phase 2 DGF study: an exploratory study following patients for 52 weeks, the data analysis will inform the Phase 3 decision on the basis of the long-term results.

Q Danielle Brill (Truist) - placebo response in myositis: consistent with immunology trials in general, site training on the primary endpoint measures helps minimise it, steroid taper built in late so as to unmask the placebo effect.

Q Yaron Werber (TD Cowen) - MG vs CIDP revenue mix: both drive growth, MG remains the larger share but both have significant potential, no precise breakdown disclosed; conviction on the seronegative approval supported by a pool estimated at ~11 000 patients and a prescriber overlap of ~80% with the existing MG base.

Q Thomas Smith (Leerink) - autoinjector timeline: manufacturing stage under way, launch expected in 2027, convenience improvement expected but less transformational than the transition to the pre-filled syringe; Graves' disease trial design in two parts, dosing on top of antithyroid drugs.

Q Akash Tewari (Jefferies) - filing strategy in myositis: the FDA decision on pooled vs by-subgroup data will depend on the results, the company will let the data guide the labelling approach; rationale for the ADAPT Forward combination (VYVGART + empasiprubart) exploratory, positive signals would guide the move into Phase 3.

Q Sean Laaman (Morgan Stanley) - first-line potential in CIDP: post-hoc analysis showing 87,5% efficacy in treatment-naive patients supports first-line positioning, conversations with payers drawing on the clinical data; IMNM: ~6-7 000 patients treated out of an addressable market of 20 000, overlap of MG/CIDP neurologists facilitating market development.
Q Yixin Gao (Evercore) - development of ARGX-213: an asset ready for Phase 3 allowing more convenient dosing, indication selection combining extension of existing approvals and new therapeutic areas.

Q Jakob Mekhael (KBC) - progress of the oral FcRn collaboration: partnership with UNP progressing well across several targets, oral format expected to broaden the market by reaching early-stage patients who prefer non-injectable options.

Q Victor Floc'h (BNP Paribas) - future Phase 3 indication strategy: VYVGART is pursuing Graves' disease, no assumption that all new indications migrate to the next-generation molecules, parallel development of ARGX-213 and ARGX-124 alongside VYVGART; out of 42 000 diagnosed CIDP patients, 24 000 treated, 12 000 on suboptimal IVIG - expansion opportunity beyond the initial addressable market of 12 000 patients.

Q John Miller (William Blair) - competitive landscape of C1 inhibitors: the early data reinforce the role of complement in CIDP, empasiprubart's C2 targeting offers best-in-class potential and positions it for indications such as DGF via dual pathway targeting.

Q Samantha Semenkow (Citi) - combination therapy strategy: the value proposition requires a substantial efficacy improvement with no safety trade-off, platform trials allow rapid testing and rapid progression into Phase 3 in the event of a positive signal.

Q Minter (analyst, Q2 seasonality vs the rest of the year) - management (Sandrine Piret-Gerard) confirms a classic post-Q1 rebound and expects a curve shape similar to prior years over the rest of the fiscal year despite the strong start of seronegative gMG.
Q Archila (Wells Fargo, status of the ocular MG file and impact on the revenue trajectory) - management says it is very confident that this indication will constitute a new long-term growth driver.

Q Thompson (Stifel, topline data expected in myositis and filing path in DM) - Karen Massey indicates that an approval would be the first FcRn authorisation in rheumatology, and that the company is looking for positive data on the primary endpoint in one or more subgroups.

Q Tiwari (Jefferies, on the size/duration of the myositis trial) - CMO Luc Truyen acknowledges that a trial twice as long and as large increases the probability of statistical significance without guaranteeing it, and that the company will determine its path once the data are read, positive or not.

Q Sharma (Goldman Sachs, read-across from the DGF study to MMN) - the CMO specifies that the Phase 2 DGF study (transplantation) was an exploratory proof-of-concept study and that its results do NOT support a DGF indication; Karen Massey adds that no causal link is to be drawn with MMN, the most important data point for MMN remaining the positive Phase 2 results on grip strength (part A and open-label extension).

Q Suneja (Guggenheim, Phase 1 profile of the ARGX-One2One IgAN programme) - the CMO says he is very enthusiastic about the Phase 1 signal, cites a positive reception from key opinion leaders, and highlights the speed and depth of the programme relative to the sector's other IgAN efforts.

Q Werber (Cowen, design of the MMN study) - the CMO confirms that the primary endpoint is grip strength, with a non-inferiority margin defined from existing IVIG data, and an option to target superiority given the Phase 2 data.

Q Truist analyst for Danielle Brill (CIDP commercial momentum vs empasiprubart trials) - the Chief Commercialization Officer confirms the intention to analyse the VYVGART and empasiprubart data jointly once the readout is available in order to refine the commercial strategy.

Q Smith (Leerink, FcRn portfolio strategy 213/124 vs VYVGART) - Karen Massey specifies that ARGX-213 has a weekly dosing schedule in Q4, that ARGX-124 is still having its differentiating advantages characterised, and that an oral FcRn programme is also progressing rapidly.

Q Semenkow (Citi, dynamics among treatment-naive CIDP patients) - the Chief Commercialization Officer indicates growing but gradual traction among naive patients, held back by entrenched prescribing habits and by payers requiring prior experience on IVIG.

Q Clark Gartner (Evercore, impact of the riliprubart news on the empasiprubart CIDP programme) - Karen Massey recalls that empasiprubart's CIDP programme comprises two distinct studies (head-to-head vs IVIG and placebo-controlled); the CMO indicates that this news reinforces his confidence on the IVIG study.
Q Flock (BNP Paribas, momentum of the pre-filled syringe and the autoinjector) - Karen Massey confirms that the VYVGART SC autoinjector remains on track for a 2027 launch.

Q RBC analyst for Luca Issey (statistical significance/alpha threshold of the myositis trials) - the CMO declines to disclose the alpha value used, specifying that even an alpha between 0,05 and 0,1 could open a regulatory discussion in these rare diseases, and confirms that the data will be available shortly.

Q Ding (Redburn, selection criteria for business development assets) - Karen Massey indicates that she is looking for assets in areas of high unmet medical need, first-in-class or best-in-class, both for the internal pipeline and for BD.

Q Xiandeng (UBS, biological rationale IMNM vs DM in myositis) - the CMO indicates that both subtypes are driven by autoantibodies but that the Phase 2 signal in DM was not explainable by the type 1 interferon pathway, justifying an approach differentiated from that of other players in the sector.

engagementsStructurants.engagement: VYVGART SC autoinjector positioned for a launch across all approved indications in 2027 - explicitly confirmed in Q&A (Flock/BNP Paribas question) as still on the planned trajectory.

Data from the Phase 3 'ASSURE' study in myositis (beyond the ALKIVIA Phase 2/3 readout, now positive - see hypothese.text) expected in the second half of 2027, the foundation of broader leadership in rheumatology according to the CEO.

hypothese.source: Event-driven refresh (17/08/2026) - positive topline readout of the Phase 3 ALKIVIA study (myositis) released today, resolving one of the two major pipeline binaries tracked since creation (see EVENTS & INFLECTIONS). A form-only refresh in the sense of the FRESHNESS CHECK: no new quarter released since Q2 26 (23-30/07/2026), sourcing for that call already complete (communiqueAnalyse/transcriptAnalyse already true) - dernierCall/guidanceHistory/data/adjXXX carried over as they stand, anchors not reopened other than a descriptive update to AN-BINAIRES-PIPELINE (no impact on the adjXXX: myositis remains outside the model, no approval/commercial launch secured at this stage). Three targeted objects for this pass: (1) incorporation of the ALKIVIA readout (primary source: argenx press release of 17/08/2026, corroborated by a sell-side note supplied by the user for the regulatory/strategic colour); (2) modernisation of coherenceQualitative to the new protocol (suiviNarratif now always populated, sens added where points is non-empty, type added on historique) - rebuilt from a COMPLETE RE-READING of the Drive files Q1 26/Q2 26 (transcript/ARGENX/) rather than from the lines already stored in historique alone, in accordance with the protocol now in force (to note: the Q1 26 Drive proved poorer in Q&A detail than the history already captured in a previous session - the two sources were cross-checked); (3) minor correction to hypothese.quarterlyEPS.PY (2025 quarterly EPS): Q3 26 corrected from 5,24$ to 5,18$ and Q4 from 8,02$ to 8,06$ after direct re-verification against argenx's primary results releases (6-K Q3 2025 and FY2025) rather than an aggregated source - Q1 (2,58$) and Q2 (3,74$) confirmed unchanged. Share price updated to 851,29$ (proxy price.php, 17/08/2026) - the decline vs the previously recorded price (1 030$) very probably predates this refresh and is not attributed to the ALKIVIA readout (not analysed here, outside the scope of this pass).

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No formal quantitative guidance (constant practice). Two registrational readouts before year-end: myositis (VYVGART, Q3 - success = positive primary in at least one subtype, IMNM/DM analyzed independently) and empasiprubart in MMN (Q4 - head-to-head vs IVIg, non-inferiority on grip strength with superiority option).
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: Stated financial profile: increasing operating margins, sustained earnings growth, significant cash generation. Vision 2030: 10 labeled indications, 5 late-stage molecules by 2030.
pointsCles: Q2 26: product sales $1.5B (+60% YoY, +17% QoQ, 18th consecutive growth quarter, beat ~$108M) - US $1.3B (+15% QoQ, stable net pricing), Japan +55% QoQ incl a ~$25M ONE-OFF from a distribution-model change; operating income $494M (+146%), cash $5.2B (+$744M YTD); EPS $7.32 beat by $1.13.

Seronegative gMG approval is the quarter's event: VYVGART now the only treatment across ALL gMG serotypes (+11,000 addressable patients), ~55% of US commercial lives covered within 10 weeks (90% targeted in 3-6 months), most plans dropping the serology-test requirement, and a measurable HALO effect on seropositive prescriptions; PFS keeps pulling new-to-brand (~80% of US PFS patients).

Two registrational readouts before year-end: myositis (rheumatology entry; IMNM and DM read independently, both framed as potential blockbusters; DM autoantibody rationale defended against the interferon thesis) and empasiprubart MMN (head-to-head vs IVIg after the Phase II showed -81% rescue need; non-inferiority on grip strength, superiority optional).

Franchise depth: >5,000 repeat prescribers, 60% of patients reaching sustained minimal symptom expression (claimed unique), >25,000 patient-years of safety; next-gen FcRn (213 Phase-III-ready Q4-weekly, 124 characterizing, ORAL FcRn advancing), ARGX-121 IgA sweeper (-90% IgA single dose) rushed into IgAN; balance sheet now widens BD scope to biotech assets - same bar: novel, de-riskable biology in high-unmet-need immunology.

hypothese.guidanceLongTerme: Vision 2030: treat 50 000 patients worldwide, obtain 10 labelled indications, advance 5 pipeline candidates into registrational development by 2030 - reaffirmed without change in Q2 26, a qualitative target not quantified financially.
hypothese.summary: VYVGART franchise still in profitable hypergrowth (revenue +60% YoY, H1 operating margin at 31% against 19% a year earlier), two regulatory binaries resolved positively (seronegative gMG, ocular MG), dilution confirmed to be close to nil. Of the two major pipeline binaries, ALKIVIA (myositis) has just resolved positively (IMNM statistically significant, DM positive but not significant); EMPASSION (MMN, Q4 26) is still to come.

ancrages.moteur: VYVGART franchise in confirmed acceleration: Q2 26 net product sales at 1 516 M$ (+60% YoY, +17% QoQ), 18th consecutive quarter of growth, driven by the launch of the broadened seronegative gMG label (approved and launched in Q2) and the first effects of the ocular MG extension (positive ADAPT OCULUS results).
Operating leverage confirmed: H1 26 operating margin at 31,1% (against 19,2% in H1 25), a scissor effect between sales and costs that continues as the VYVGART franchise scales.

One of the two major binary catalysts has just resolved: ALKIVIA (myositis) topline readout released on 17/08/2026, positive and statistically significant on the combined IMNM/DM population (TIS benefit +15,4 pts vs placebo, p=0,0011) and on the IMNM subtype alone (+14,8 pts, p=0,0048 - first positive Phase 3 in an indication with no approved treatment); positive but non-significant signal in DM (+14,5 pts, p=0,1093, insufficient sample size). IMNM regulatory filing expected to be prioritised according to the sell-side note (not confirmed by a primary press release at this stage); DM path still to be defined with the authorities. EMPASSION (MMN, Q4 26 readout) remains the second catalyst, entirely unresolved. BOTH remain EXCLUDED from the adjXXX (no approval or commercial launch secured) - treatment unchanged in its logic, but the risk profile of the myositis franchise is genuinely de-risked vs the previous reading.

Dilution confirmed to be close to nil: H1 26 average diluted shares at 64,4M (slightly down vs 65,6M in H1 25) - the thesis of self-funded financing with no new capital raise is validated, even slightly better than expected.

Cash position (cash + equivalents + current financial assets) up to 5,2 Md$ at 30/06/2026 (against 4,4 Md$ at end-2025), H1 26 operating cash flow clearly positive (+0,7 Md$ against -0,4 Md$ in H1 25) - a faster cash generation trajectory than expected, available for BD/licensing in line with the Vision 2030 ambition.

Broadening of the pipeline beyond the catalysts already tracked: registrational study launched in Graves' disease, positive signal from the Phase 2 VARVARA study (empasiprubart, delayed graft function in transplantation) at 52 weeks, ten molecules expected to be in clinical development by end-2026 - positive optionality not quantified in the model.

Governance transition completed: Karen Massey (former COO since March 2023) appointed CEO in May 2026, with founder Tim Van Hauwermeiren becoming non-executive Chairman of the Board - strategic continuity asserted (Vision 2030 reaffirmed without change), 90,9% of the capital represented at the 2026 AGM in support.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
The profitable-growth compounder thesis strengthens: H1 26 net product sales 2,813M (+62% YoY), operating margin 31.1% (vs 19.2%) - operating leverage materializing faster than modeled at setup. Two regulatory binaries resolved POSITIVELY in Q2: the VYVGART/Hytrulo gMG label extended to ALL serotypes (seronegative included, US launch underway) and ADAPT OCULUS read out positive, opening ocular MG. Dilution remains near zero; net cash builds from 4.7bn toward ~15bn by 2030.

== THESIS READ ==
- VYVGART is compounding across indications on a single commercial engine - each label extension lands on an existing cost base. Watch: seronegative/ocular launch uptake in US scripts.
- EMPASSION (MMN) topline expected Q4 26 is now the last fully-open major pipeline binary. Watch: the readout - it swings the 2028+ trajectory.
- The 17/08 event pass (ALKIVIA integration into coherence tracking) changed no numbers - projections stand on the 03/08 refresh. Watch: IMNM regulatory filing calendar (breakthrough designation to confirm at source).

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
GAAP base in USD ('ca' = net product sales, 'ebit' = published IFRS operating profit). FY24-FY25 published nets are inflated by deferred-tax-asset recognition (FY24: net 832M on a NEGATIVE -30M EBIT) - documented in the bridge; projections use a 15% normative rate. Dilution near zero confirmed.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: sales 6.4bn, EBIT 2,043M (margin ~32%), net 1,943M / EPS 29.89 (on consensus). 2027-2030: sales +18-20%/yr fading, margin toward 42%; finNet = interest income on the growing net cash (~4.4%). Watch: EMPASSION; Q3 sales split by region; ETR normalization path as DTA amortizes.

== CATALYSTS ==
EMPASSION topline (Q4 26); seronegative gMG launch curve; IMNM filing; FY26 results (Feb/Mar 2027).
